checks.detail: R/n^(3/4) for the staircase RISES to a peak at n=55 (1.225167) and falls afterwards to 0.7321169 at n=1830. So this statistic is not monotone for a Theta(sqrt n) object, and a flat reading near the peak carries no information about the rate.

over n=36..78 the staircase R/n^(3/4) varies by only 2.08% (1.19971, 1.2189, 1.22517, 1.2158). The M_n scan covers n=40..76 and shows the same flatness at the same value (~1.24). A provably Theta(sqrt n) object is therefore INDISTINGUISHABLE from Theta(n^(3/4)) on this statistic over exactly the reachable range.

the staircase's R/sqrt(n) is 4.4655872 at n=435, still 12.37% short of its PROVED limit 5.0959457 — at ten times the largest enumerable n. So a rising M/sqrt(n) is exactly what a Theta(sqrt n) object looks like here and is not evidence against it.

the control only becomes decisive past n ~ 150, where the staircase ratio has clearly left its peak. p(84) = 26,543,660 (reached, ~50 min); p(150) = 40,853,235,313 — a factor of 1,539, about three orders of magnitude. Enumeration is out of reach at the scale that would decide the question.

conclusion: the M/n^{3/4}-vs-M/sqrt(n) discriminator does not discriminate at reachable n; a provably Theta(sqrt n) control shows the same flatness over the same range. Sharpness is closed to enumeration.
